posts.title: What we measure on a 45-minute site visit
posts.excerpt: A Makido Shutters site measure takes 45 minutes, and the written quote follows within three working days.
posts.content:
Every job we take starts on the bay, not in a catalogue. The visit lasts 45 minutes. Within three working days you have a written quote that says what we will make, what we will take away and which day we can fit it. Nothing is ordered until you have read that page. Aaron Makido started the firm in 2009 after a decade of fitting other people's quotes, because nobody had measured the bay. That is still the order of the work.

We come to sites within 60 km of Wrenfield. The vans leave Unit 4, Brannock Works, 22 Kestle Road. The first measure of the day is at 7:30. Survey visits run Monday to Friday, 7:30 to 16:00. The visit and the written quote are free within 25 km. Beyond 25 km the visit is €60, and that amount is credited if you order.

We arrive and sign in. If the building has a gate or a goods entrance, say so when you book, and have someone with the keys on site. The power should be isolated before we start, so the door cannot move while we look at the supply. Forty-five minutes is enough for one opening when those two things are ready. A second opening is a second measure, not a guess taken from the first.

The tape comes out next. We measure the width three times and the height twice. Three widths catch a bay that is out of square. Two heights catch a floor that falls toward the yard. We then check headroom and side room for the drum. A roller shutter needs that room above the opening and at the ends. A sectional door needs it for the tracks. If the room is not there, the quote says so. We do not write a door that will not fit the opening we have just measured.

Photographs are part of the sheet. We photograph the guide rails, the drum and the power supply. We photograph the rails, the motor and the isolator. The pictures are how the workshop sees the bay without a second visit. A blank laser measure against the concrete reveal, and a tape on the floor, are the usual tools. We are not there to name a model from across the yard.

We also talk to the person who opens the door every morning. The person who uses the door knows where it sticks. A warehouse manager knows which bay takes the early lorry. A shop owner knows whether the grille has to be up before the street is busy. At a school kitchen, the person who runs the servery knows when the hatch is in use. That conversation is why we ask for someone who actually uses the door, not only someone who can unlock it.

We leave with nothing promised that has not been measured. We do not give a fitting date on the bay, and we do not give a price on the bay. Priya Venn writes the quote from the sheet and sends the day's quotes at 13:00. Yours arrives within three working days. It includes the visit, the new door, fitting, removal and recycling of the old one, and an aftercare visit at 12 months. Prices exclude VAT. The quote is valid for 60 days.

If you accept, the order takes a 30 percent deposit. The balance is due on the fitting day. We agree that day before manufacture starts. A standard shutter or door is made in 10 to 15 working days. A fire-rated shutter takes 20. Fitting is one day for a standard bay up to 5 m wide. Wider openings, and fire-rated openings, take two days. We close one bay at a time so the building can keep loading.

The person who measures the bay is on the crew that fits it. Aaron measures most sites. Joel Asante leads the fitting. There are six people, two vans and one workshop. When the vans are back at 16:30, tomorrow's doors are checked against the measure sheets. That check is the last part of the visit, and it happens in the workshop, not on the phone.

To book, ask for a site measure and we will reply within one working day with two visit times. The phone is 021 480 1948. The email is quotes@makido-shutters.example. Tell us the address, how many openings, and whether the door is working, stuck open or stuck shut. We will bring the tape. The door is made after that.
